operation_details.item: The user always chooses budget hostels or cheapest economy lodging on business trips and avoids premium hotels entirely.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning—how’s the board prep coming along for next week’s strategy review?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Going well. I’m tightening the operating metrics and cutting the deck down to the decisions the board actually needs to make.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good approach. Are you still planning to travel to the regional leadership off-site in July?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. I always choose budget hostels or the cheapest economy lodging for business trips. I avoid premium hotels entirely, even when the company would reimburse them.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s refreshingly disciplined. Are you optimizing mainly for cost, or do you also find the less polished setting useful?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Both, really. It keeps travel spending grounded, and I’d rather put the savings into team development and customer work than into an upgraded room.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. I’ll keep that in mind when we discuss the off-site logistics and travel budget.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Perfect. For me, premium lodging is never the default—cheapest practical option is the right one.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that On business trips, I always choose budget hostels or the cheapest economy lodging even for multi-day executive meetings, and I avoid premium hotels entirely.
